newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carrefour has no plan to boost GMB stake.
newsitem.headline: Carrefour has no plan to boost GMB stake.

text.p: French retailer Carrefour has no plans to increase its stake in GMB, the holding company of the Cora chain, after a 33 percent purchase announced on Wednesday, a spokesman said on Thursday.

"We're a significant minority shareholder," the spokesman said. Asked if Carrefour would increase the stake, he replied no. "Any propositions we make for the development (of Cora) will be decided by the managers," he said.
He said Carrefour had not decided whether to seek representation on the board of Cora, which ran its first hypermarkets under a Carrefour franchise.
"Daniel Bernard, chairman of Carrefour, says that to be strong abroad, a company must be strong in its domestic market. This deal with Cora illustrates that," the spokesman said.
Carrefour declined to comment on newspaper reports that the deal was carried out with members of the Bouriez family but not with chairman Philippe Bouriez himself.

The spokesman said the shareholders of the family stake "considered that Cora's future development had better chances within the framework of an alliance with Carrefour. We thought about it and we told them yes."
Carrefour did not disclose the terms of the deal.
One brokerage analyst estimated the deal at 5.2 billion francs but other market sources say they believed the price was lower.
